subject.title: fix(reef): bound relay HTTP JSON response body reads

question: Can every supported Reef relay success response for authentication, friends, mail pull/send, and acknowledgement be guaranteed below 16 MiB, or must one or more endpoints use a different limit or pagination contract?
rationale: The bounded-reader implementation is sound, but repository docs and the available relay contract do not prove that 16 MiB is safe for all existing deployments; selecting the compatibility ceiling requires Reef protocol ownership.

options.title: Confirm the 16 MiB contract
options.body: Verify that relay-side limits or pagination keep every supported success response below 16 MiB, document or test that invariant, and merge this patch.

options.title: Use endpoint-specific ceilings
options.body: Keep bounded streaming reads but assign limits according to each relay endpoint's documented maximum response shape.

options.title: Accept the client-only cutoff
options.body: Merge the 16 MiB ceiling as an intentional fail-closed compatibility change and own the possibility that unusually large existing pulls stop working.

recommendation.title: Confirm the 16 MiB contract
recommendation.body: Verify that relay-side limits or pagination keep every supported success response below 16 MiB, document or test that invariant, and merge this patch.

likelyOwner.reason: Their merged Reef guard-response hardening is the closest recent owner-level work on Reef response-size contracts.
